bull_thesis: Zealand Pharma is a partner-validated amylin franchise priced as an option on imminent clinical de-risking, sitting on a fortress balance sheet. The thesis rests on five evidence-grounded pillars. (1) THE ROCHE ALLIANCE (Q1-2025) is the strongest external endorsement available to a pre-commercial biotech: co-development, co-commercialization, 50/50 profit share in the US and EU, plus access to Roche's CT-388 (GLP-1/GIP) for a fixed-dose combo. This is real downside cushion against catalyst slippage and funds the run into Phase III. (3) THE AMYLIN MECHANISM IS DE-RISKED BY A RIVAL'S DATA: cagrilintide's Phase III (June 2025) showed clean GI tolerability and no unexpected safety signals, which management correctly framed as a 'major derisking event' for the class - petrelintide shares the human-amylin backbone and a similar receptor profile. bear_thesis: This is a pure binary clinical bet mislabeled 'deep_value,' with no margin of safety, two CORRELATED catalysts firing in the same window, and the single most important question dodged by management for a year. (1) THE 'VALUE' SIGNAL IS AN ARTIFACT. The screener's FY-2025 figures - revenue +14,598.9%, gross margin 99.7%, net margin 70.0%, EPS 90.22, NI +6.46B - are NOT operating results; they are the one-time accounting recognition of the Roche upfront/milestones. Petrelintide's pivotal ZUPREME-1 42-week Phase II and survodutide's SYNCHRONIZE-1 Phase III BOTH read out in H1-2026 - and they are not independent resolution drivers: both ride the same obesity/amylin/incretin-class sentiment and the same regulatory-scientific TAM narrative. consensus_delta: Reframed for a 'deep_value' label that does not fit the asset: the street is NOT pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power - there is no stable earnings power to mis-price. Critically, the one factually contestable street assumption - that petrelintide's 15-20% target is near-locked - is exactly what management has NOT proven and has deflected for four quarters (the 4.8mg-approximately-9mg dose-response flattening in males). That cuts AGAINST a long: it is an unpriced DOWNSIDE risk, not an unpriced upside. Net: the alpha lives in the un-read clinical data, not in a market misperception a moderator can arbitrage. forcing_function: The hard-dated forcing events are clinical, not corporate: (1) ZUPREME-1 42-week Phase II top-line data for petrelintide - guided 'first half of 2026' - the single most important print; it adjudicates the 15-20% weight-loss target, the dose-response durability at BMI ~37, and the GI-tolerability differentiation that the entire 'foundational therapy' thesis rests on. The shareholder base is specialist healthcare/biotech funds and crossover/growth holders drawn in by the Roche deal and the obesity-TAM narrative, not passive income investors, so the mechanical 'pivot forces liquidation' thesis does not apply on the upside catalyst. moderator_conclusion: PASS (C), conviction 2 - applying the current regime, this is a high-quality company in the regime's worst lane with correlated binaries and no margin of safety. interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Zealand Pharma A/S (ZEAL.CO)
*Interrogator: Claude Opus 4.8 · Signal type as filed: "deep_value" (Healthcare) · Coverage window: Q1-2024 → FY-2025 (8 consecutive calls, 2024-05-16 → 2026-02-19)*

> **Threshold caveat the director must absorb first.** This company is filed as "deep_value," but the transcript is unambiguous: Zealand is a **pre-commercial, partner-funded clinical-stage obesity/metabolic biotech**. Its product revenue is effectively zero; the screener's "Revenue +14,598.9% YoY," "Gross margin 99.7%," "Net margin 70.0%," "EPS 90.22," "NI 6.46B" for FY2025 are **not operating results** — they are the accounting echo of the **Roche petrelintide licensing deal** (upfront + milestone recognition, DKK-denominated) booked into a single fiscal year. Every "value" ratio derived from those lines (P/FCF 24.8x, FCF 70.5%, the "fair value 75.6" DCF) is therefore an artifact, not a margin-of-safety signal. The genuine thesis is **binary clinical catalysts**, not earnings power. I assess the narrative on that basis.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story tightened and de-risked across eight quarters, then narrowed by deliberate amputation.

**Q1-2024 (May) — "extremely exciting next few months," everything is live.** Management opened with a broad, optionality-rich pipeline: petrelintide (amylin monotherapy), dapiglutide (GLP-1/GLP-2 dual agonist), survodutide (partnered to Boehringer, MASH + obesity), two rare-disease assets at PDUFA in Q4-2024 (dasiglucagon in congenital hyperinsulinism; glepaglutide in short bowel syndrome), plus preclinical Kv1.3 and complement C3 inflammation shots. The tone was "many irons in the fire, all heating up." Runway had just been extended "into '27" via a January private placement.

**Q2-2024 (Aug) — the petrelintide readout lands and becomes the spine.** Positive Phase 1b 16-week data (4.8% / 8.6% / 8.3% weight loss across cohorts, vs 1.7% placebo) triggered a **DKK 7bn equity raise — "the largest ever European biotech offering."** From here, the story visibly re-centers on petrelintide as "a future backbone therapy," with the explicit 15–20% weight-loss target introduced for Phase III. Survodutide's MASH Phase II (fibrosis benefit, FDA Breakthrough Therapy) became the second pillar.

**Q3-2024 (Nov) → FY-2024 (Feb-2025) — building the org for a company they don't yet have.** ZUPREME-1 Phase IIb initiated (Dec-2024), 494 patients, 5 dose arms to 9mg. Commercial (Eric Cox, CCO) and scientific (Utpal Singh, CSO, ex-Lilly 18yrs) hires signal a deliberate shift from "get the data" to "be ready to commercialize." Glepaglutide hits a regulatory wall: management concedes "we are quite certain that we need to do" **another Phase III** in the US (a delay, framed calmly).

**Q1-2025 (May) — the franchise-maker: the Roche alliance.** "Zealand has never been in a stronger position than we are today." The **Roche petrelintide deal** — co-development, co-commercialization, **50/50 profit share in US + Europe**, plus access to Roche's CT-388 (GLP-1/GIP) for a fixed-dose combo — is the single most consequential event in the window. It removes the two existential biotech risks: financing and manufacturing/commercial build (Roche owns capex for supply). The narrative pivots from "promising molecule" to "leading amylin franchise."

**Q2-2025 (Aug) → Q3-2025 (Nov) — confidence hardens; the portfolio is pruned.** Cagrilintide Phase III data (Novo) is repeatedly invoked as a **"major derisking event"** for the amylin *class*. Then the disciplined cut: **dapiglutide is paused** (Q3-2025) — the "most differentiated GLP-1-containing mid-stage candidate" sacrificed because the GLP-1 lane is "increasingly crowded" and the differentiation bar for a 2030s launch is "long, complex and expensive." Dasiglucagon (CHI) hits a third-party manufacturing classification snag; contingency supplier qualified.

**FY-2025 (Feb-2026) — "the most defining and catalyst-rich year in Zealand's history."** Two hard binary readouts are teed up for **H1-2026: ZUPREME-1 42-week Phase II (petrelintide)** and **SYNCHRONIZE-1 76-week Phase III (survodutide obesity)**, plus a cardiovascular-outcomes component. A GIP analog is *restarted*; a Boston high-throughput/AI research hub and a "10 candidates into the clinic in 5 years / 5 launches in 5 years" generational-biotech ambition are introduced.

**Net arc:** broad-and-hopeful → single-asset-validated → **partner-de-risked** → portfolio-disciplined → **catalyst-gated**. Growth drivers *added*: Roche alliance, CT-388 combo, survodutide CVOT, GIP restart, AI/discovery platform. Growth drivers *dropped*: dapiglutide (paused), salmon-calcitonin/early inflammation shots (de-emphasized). The thesis is now almost entirely **"does petrelintide's Phase II confirm 15–20% with clean GI tolerability, and does survodutide's Phase III deliver."**

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The central forensic finding: **the financials provided are a deal-distorted snapshot that does not describe an operating business.** The job is to separate signal (cash runway, partner economics) from noise (the one-year revenue/EPS spike).

| Management claim | What the call said | What the financials show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| "Strong/strongest-ever financial position; funded toward profitability" | Q1-25, Q3-25: cash ~DKK 9bn at start of 2025; "can easily fund Phase II"; Roche covers manufacturing | **Net cash ≈ −14.05B (net cash, live 2026-03-31 correction); net debt −2.12B (scan)**; Altman-Z 18.4 (solvency fortress); TTM FCF +6.32B | **CORROBORATED — but for the wrong reason.** The cash and "positive FCF" are **partnership inflows (Roche upfront/milestones), not operations.** Balance-sheet strength is real and is the load-bearing fact; the "earnings" are not recurring. |
| "Transformational growth" | FY-25: rev 9.21B, NI 6.46B, EPS 90.22 vs prior-year losses | Multi-year line: 2021 NI −1.02B, 2022 −966M, 2023 −704M, 2024 −1.08B, **2025 +6.46B** | **MISLEADING IF READ AS OPERATING.** Four straight years of ~DKK 700M–1.08B net losses, then a single +6.46B year that exactly coincides with the Roche deal. This is a **one-off recognition event**, not an inflection in commercial earnings. Forward consensus EPS growth **−60.5%** confirms the market expects the spike to reverse. |
| "Best-in-class petrelintide; 15–20% weight loss" | Every call since Q2-24; reaffirmed Q3-25, FY-25 | No commercial revenue; ROE **−48.3%**, ROIC **−24.9%** (true underlying returns on the *operating* base are deeply negative) | **UNVERIFIABLE / FORWARD.** The efficacy claim rests on a **48-patient Phase 1b** (predominantly male, low BMI) — management itself flags these as response-muting. The pivotal 494-patient ZUPREME-1 42-week data **has not read out** as of the last call. Claim is a hypothesis, not a result. |
| "Amylin class de-risked by cagrilintide Phase III" | Q2-25, Q3-25 | n/a (no Zealand financial line tests this) | **PARTIALLY VALID.** True that a *competitor's* long-acting amylin showing clean GI tolerability de-risks the **mechanism**. It does **not** de-risk petrelintide's *molecule-specific* dose-response, which only ZUPREME-1 can. Management is borrowing a rival's data to backstop its own un-read trial — legitimate but not a substitute. |
| "Disciplined capital allocation" (dapiglutide pause) | Q3-25: paused "most differentiated GLP-1 candidate" on ROI grounds | Net cash positive; can afford to be selective | **CORROBORATED & CREDIBLE.** Killing a sunk-cost asset because the *launch-decade* differentiation bar is too high is exactly the discipline you want from a cash-rich pre-revenue biotech. Genuine green flag (see §6). |
| "Beat 4/7 quarters (57%)" | Screener metric | EPS "beat" is meaningless for a pre-revenue biotech whose EPS is dominated by deal timing and non-cash items | **NOT MEANINGFUL.** Earnings-beat rate has no informational content here; do not weight it. |

**Bottom line for §2:** the only financial facts that survive scrutiny are (a) a **fortress balance sheet / net-cash position** funded by partners, and (b) **deeply negative underlying operating returns** masked by one-time deal income. The valuation models (DCF "fair value 75.6," P/FCF 24.8x, all per-method MOS at −100%) are **non-operative** for a binary-catalyst biotech and should be discarded, not interpreted as a 0% / negative margin of safety "value" signal.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY — **RISING (then plateauing at high confidence)**

| Quarter | Representative language | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Q1-2024 | "extremely exciting next few months… key clinical results from all our programs" | Optimistic, broad, event-anticipatory |
| Q2-2024 | "largest ever European biotech offering… transformational potential" | Confidence + capital validation |
| Q3-2024 | "consistently demonstrated best-in-class potential" | First use of "best-in-class" as settled fact |
| FY-2024 | "transformational year… strongest possible foundation" | Self-congratulatory, forward-leaning |
| Q1-2025 | **"Zealand has never been in a stronger position than we are today"** | Peak conviction — the Roche-deal high |
| Q2-2025 | "exceedingly well positioned… major derisking event" | Sustained high confidence |
| Q3-2025 | "strong execution and continued momentum… catalyst-rich chapter" | Confident *and* disciplined (pause framed as strength) |
| FY-2025 | **"the most defining and catalyst-rich year in Zealand's history"** | Confidence intact, now explicitly betting on H1-2026 readouts |

**Direction:** clearly **Rising** Q1-24 → Q1-25, then **stable-high** through FY-25. Crucially, the language stayed **offensive (growth/investment/franchise-building)** throughout — there is **no defensive pivot** to cost/efficiency/macro-survival, which is the tell you watch for in deteriorating biotechs. Guidance *specificity* on clinical timelines stayed high and consistent (42-week data H1-26, Phase III H2-26). The one area where specificity was deliberately *withheld* is financial runway: Henriette Wennicke, Q1-25 — **"you don't really guide on the runway anymore"** — a notable, repeated non-answer (see §5).

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY — **MEDIUM-HIGH on clinical/operational; LOW-information on financial**

This is a biotech, so "guidance" = clinical timelines and trial-execution promises, not revenue guides. On that axis the track record is **good**:

- **Petrelintide Phase 1b** (promised Q2-2024) → **delivered** on time, positive, Q2-2024. ✅
- **DKK 7bn raise** (capability claimed) → **executed**, oversubscribed, Q2-2024. ✅
- **ZUPREME-1 initiation** (guided H2-2024) → **first patient dosed Dec-2024**; enrollment completed **ahead of schedule** ("significantly faster than initially anticipated"). ✅ (genuine over-delivery on enrollment pace)
- **Roche partnership** (telegraphed as "initiating dialogues" Q2-2024) → **signed Q1-2025**, on the strategic terms management had publicly insisted on (50/50, retained commercial rights). ✅ Management said it would only accept a partner who would "win, not just play," and "maintain rights in major markets" — and the realized deal matched that stated red line. Promise→delivery integrity is **high**.
- **28-week ZUPREME-1 primary-endpoint visit** (guided) → **completed late Sept-2025**, on track. ✅

**Misses / slips:**
- **Glepaglutide**: implied a clean US path early; by FY-2024 conceded a **full additional Phase III** is required (material timeline slip, but disclosed promptly and calmly). 🔴/neutral.
- **Dasiglucagon (CHI)**: PDUFA-era optimism (Q1-2024) → by Q3-2025 a **third-party manufacturing classification has *not* been upgraded**, forcing a contingency supplier. A real, unresolved operational drag on a near-term approvable asset. 🔴.
- **Dapiglutide**: progressed confidently for six quarters, then **paused**. Defensible on merits, but anyone who underwrote dapi optionality took a write-down.

**Sandbagging?** No evidence of lowballing. If anything management is **aspirational-high** (the "5 launches in 5 years / 10 INDs in 5 years" framing at FY-25 is a stretch target, not a sandbag). **Reliability: Medium-High** on what they control (trial execution, deal-making), **caveated** by two rare-disease execution stumbles and a financial-runway information vacuum.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts circled the same few soft spots repeatedly:

1. **The weight-loss curve "tailing off" at high dose / the 4.8mg vs 9mg non-separation.** Thomas Bowers (Danske, Q3-24) and Carsten Lønborg Madsen (Danske, Q2-25) both pressed: doubling the dose from 4.8→9mg produced **no clear additional response in males**, and the curve looked like it flattened after ~week 12–13. Management's answer was consistently "small study, low-BMI male population, individual variability — Phase II will resolve it." This is the **single most important open question**, and it is precisely what ZUPREME-1's 42-week readout will adjudicate. Management is asking investors to trust that a 48-patient signal scales to 494 patients at higher BMI. *If the Phase II shows the same dose-response flattening, the "best-in-class / 15–20%" thesis is impaired.*
2. **Financial runway.** Multiple analysts (Laura Hindley/Morgan Stanley; others) asked what the cash supports through Phase III. CFO repeatedly declined: **"you don't really guide on the runway anymore."** For a company whose entire thesis depends on funding through expensive Phase III + pre-launch build, the refusal to frame runway is a persistent, deliberate opacity.
3. **Combination-therapy GI tolerability compounding.** Mohit Bansal (Wells Fargo, Q3-25) pushed the sharpest scientific challenge: amylin *itself* has GI effects; stacking it with a GLP-1/GIP (CT-388) could **compound** tolerability problems — undercutting the entire "better patient experience" differentiator. Management's "we max the amylin and add only a teaspoon of GLP-1" answer is a hypothesis, untested in humans for this combo (Phase II only starts H1-2026).
4. **Partner economics / cost-share caps.** Ollie Burrow (Goldman, Q1-25) probed whether Zealand has uncapped R&D cost exposure under the Roche 50/50. Management confirmed it **shares R&D cost** (Roche carries manufacturing capex) but **declined to quantify Zealand's spend** — leaving the magnitude of Zealand's funding obligation genuinely unclear.
5. **Competitive encroachment in amylin** (Lilly eloralintide, Novo cagrilintide/CagriSema, AbbVie/Boehringer). Asked every call. Management's posture shifted from "we're unique" → "we welcome competition, it validates the class" — a reasonable but convenient reframe (see §7).

**Pattern:** the deflected/under-answered topics (runway, cost-share magnitude, dose-response durability) are all **the ones that would matter most in a downside scenario.** None has yet "turned into bad news" except glepaglutide (foreshadowed) and dasiglucagon manufacturing.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director) — **STRENGTHENING (binary-gated)**

**Classification: STRENGTHENING.** Over eight quarters Zealand converted a hopeful multi-asset pipeline into a **partner-validated, well-capitalized, disciplined amylin franchise** with a credible second shot (survodutide) carried at someone else's cost.
